item.title: Survey: P2P Signaling and Relay Server Technologies
item.description:
Building a self-hosted P2P signaling and relay server is the core infrastructure for cross-network connectivity, remote access, and mesh VPN scenarios. This article systematically surveys the complete technology landscape across three dimensions: protocol standards (STUN/TURN/ICE/BEHAVE), mainstream products (Tailscale, Nebula, NetBird, ZeroTier, Headscale, OpenZiti, etc.), and frameworks & algorithms (libp2p, WebRTC, Kademlia DHT).

All technical descriptions are verified against primary sources—RFC originals, academic papers, and official documentation. Key statistics include citations.

item.title: Third-Party Free P2P Nodes: Public STUN, Free TURN Quotas, and Community Relays
item.description: When it comes time to provision NAT traversal for a P2P application, “just use someone else’s free nodes” is the most commonly suggested route. In practice, most third-party P2P networks cannot be connected to at all: node discovery, authentication, traversal coordination, and the encrypted handshake are each governed by the network designer’s own private protocol. Without implementing that protocol stack, your first packet never goes out. Only three categories of nodes are open to any application and free of charge: public STUN, free TURN quotas, and community relay networks.
